items.tweet_text:
In a first-of-its-kind partnership between state and federal partners, ICE Miami and Florida law enforcement arrested nearly 800 illegal aliens this week during the first four days of #OperationTidalWave — a massive, multi-agency, immigration enforcement crackdown.

💡Learn how law enforcement agencies can partner with us at http://ICE.gov/287g

🔊@CBP provided extraordinary support during this operation. We appreciate our @DHSgov partner's commitment to public safety.

📷Check out the first photos from the field of this highly successful operation.

description.text: A plain candid operational photograph from Operation Tidal Wave with no on-image text, slogans, or agency seal overlay. Shot outdoors in a sunny residential area (white stucco buildings, green hedges, palm fronds, an air-conditioning condenser unit), it shows officers escorting a handcuffed man up a grassy strip between buildings, all photographed from behind. The detained man in the center wears a white t-shirt printed with an American flag and is flanked by two agents in tactical vests: one vest reads 'POLICE / ICE,' the other reads 'FBI / POLICE'; a third heavily armed tactical officer is at far left. The image documents a multi-agency immigration arrest. Tweet context describes ICE Miami and Florida law enforcement arresting nearly 800 illegal aliens during #OperationTidalWave.

transcript.text: On January 28th, 2025, following an executive order, securing our borders issued by President Trump, USCIS stopped accepting new cases in a variety of categorical parole programs established by the previous administration. USCIS reviews categorical parole processes. USCIS is restoring the original intent of immigration parole. We have issued more than half a million notices to aliens from Cuba, Haiti, Nicaragua, and Venezuela, informing them of the termination of their parole and employment authorization under the CHNV, parole program effective April 24th, and encouraging them to report their departure from the country with the CBP home app. We are committed to supporting DHS efforts to implement more prudent, durable, and appropriate measures to enhance the security of our borders. For more information, visit USCIS.gov.
